lens: Product value and pilot fit on the current website (D27-D29): value to office and crews, phone reach, pilot and roadmap order, crews' screen unchanged, honesty, demo with labelled data, and what the owner asked for
status: Judgement only; the only file written. design-a/b/c.json and plan-critique-product.json carry no review key, so their facts are unreviewed; the facts relied on were re-checked live or in the repo (facts_rechecked).
rubric: Sub-scores 0-10, weights: V value to office and crews on the current product [3]; P pilot fit and roadmap order, crews' screen unchanged [2]; F phone and field reach [2]; H honesty traps avoided [2]; D demo with labelled data [1]; O owner's ask versus delivered [1]. Score = sum(weight x sub-score) / 11.
bottom_line: design-c ranks first. It is the only one of the three a crew could open on a phone (public site, live HTTP 200, viewport tag), it needs no installer, parked app or new library, and its build flag keeps the crews' screen unchanged. design-a and design-b score low: crews cannot reach them, and both need the owner to reverse D27 (DECISIONS.md:314-323). None of the three answers the site's three questions (DESIGN.md:16-19) better than the Now, town and reports pages. The biggest crew gaps (alerts to phones, ROADMAP Next 12; a MESH hail footprint, Next 11; job context, DECISIONS.md:324-325) are in none of the designs.
frame: Current product: the website (AGENTS.md:7-12; DECISIONS.md:314-321). The desktop app is parked (AGENTS.md:13-14; ROADMAP Next 15, lines 80-82). design-a and design-b were written for the parked app and its self-test, 50 MiB and installer constraints; this judgement asks what each would mean for the product as it stands.

Crew reach: DESIGN.md:22-23 names 'a crew lead on a phone in a truck or on a roof'. DESIGN.md:12-14 records that the app asked crews to install software. ROADMAP Next 2 (lines 40-43) makes the pilot a feedback week with checks on an iPhone and an Android phone.

scores.name: Design C: Python-first 2.5D on the flat map (C2 first; C1 globe gated to Phase 5)
reasons: F 9: the public site is phone-viewport ready (live check, 2026-10-17); DECISIONS.md:353 gives 'works on any phone' as the reason for the website. C2 adds no installer, library or server (website.yml:80 already installs numpy and pygrib). Not tested on a phone (DECISIONS.md:402-403).

P 7: the default build writes no echo, cloud or transect files (design-c.json default_off_setting), so the crews' screen is unchanged unless it is turned on. Held back because its feeds (MRMS levels, GOES ACHA, Band 13) come before ROADMAP Next 4.

V 5, low to medium: echo-top classes and three transects add to the radar loop the site already shows (DESIGN.md:295). The critique rates the near-echo job 'low' and the coverage job 'medium'; C serves part of the second. Cloud-top height has no decision link: the weather handoff's Live Storms layers (line 29) have no clouds.

H 7: reuses the no-coverage rule. Negative MRMS rates are no coverage, hatched, never dry (gridded.py:192-197, 340-345; DESIGN.md:275-276). Legends say 'not hail, not damage' and 'not an all-clear' (design-c.json legend_echo). Stop rules hide the echo layer (P2) or keep only the echo raster (P3). Docked for uncorrected cloud tops (parallax.json, 3-33 km off).
D 5: silent on demo, but the labelled sample build (base.html:17) could carry the new layers with little extra work.

O 3: no globe and no 3D volumes in the first build (design-c.json sub_options). The latest recorded map instruction is a flat, Apple-Weather-style Montana map (DECISIONS.md:359-362, D28), which C extends.

Gate mismatch: passes need n of at least 20 and are report-only below (evaluation-predeclared.json lines 19-20); DESIGN.md:35 uses 5 users; the pilot has two named users (Next 2). Under C's own gates the echo layer stays report-only through the pilot.

Dependency: the one-hour echo window needs frames kept between builds (ROADMAP Next 6, not built). load_previous (build.py:472) serves last-known alerts (help text, line 485), so frame reuse is new code.
fatal_flaws: Owner decision, ROADMAP Next 4: new feeds before predeclared metrics exist ('before any new feed is added', ROADMAP.md:46-48; review P0 'Not started', line 89). Carson must order it behind Next 4, or the flagged build stays on a branch.

Owner or counsel decision, site-wide: GitHub's Additional Product Terms say 'don't use Actions as a content delivery network' and 'You may only access and use GitHub Actions to develop and test your application(s)' (WebFetch, 2026-10-17). The site already publishes this way (D27); C adds about 0.66 MB per build to it (design-c.json size_impact). Gate new product files on this decision.
Owner decision: P1 showing uncorrected cloud tops (design-c.json owner_decisions). The displacement (3-33 km) is the largest honesty risk in the set; hold the cloud layer until Phase 2.
Owner decision, scope: no 3D in the first build (design-c.json sub_options). README.md section 2 D-G1 was written for the app and needs rewording for the website.

scores.name: Design A: CesiumJS page inside the parked Flask app (/globe)
reasons: O 8: the closest match to the literal ask: a CesiumJS globe, cloud tops lifted by ACHA height after parallax correction (phase 2), voxel storms (phase 3, at least 35 dBZ by default, below-ground cells dropped) (design-a.json phases, storms_3d_rules). Imagery is USGS and GIBS, not photorealistic.

F 0: the app's server binds 127.0.0.1 (desktop/launcher.py:433) and every route needs the window cookie (DECISIONS.md:23-29, D2). design-a.json never mentions phones, so the pilot's phone checks (Next 2) cannot run on it.

P 2: serving /globe from the parked app means reviving it (DECISIONS.md:322-323; Next 15), and phases 1-3 add new feeds before Next 4. Crews would have to install the desktop app again; D27 replaced that with a site that needs nothing installed (DESIGN.md:12-14, 51).

V 3: the 3D view adds perspective to the radar the site already loops; its time loop (phase 4) repeats the past-hour timeline (DESIGN.md:295). Job context lives in the parked app (DECISIONS.md:324-325).

H 6: strong labels and a parity test against alert_targets on at least 20 fixtures (design-a.json alert_null_geometry). Docked for 3x and 5x exaggeration (the 'stretched' label is the only guard) and the bundled ion token and D26/D27 numbering.
D 3: excludes demo data in every phase (design-a.json storms_3d_rules). Rule 5 would allow DEMO-labelled data, so the owner walkthrough the critique rates medium is lost.

Weight: Cesium.js alone is 6,080,574 B raw and 1,778,166 B over the wire with gzip (live). Voxel frames are 9.44 MB at 20 dBZ and 1.52 MB at 35 dBZ (computed: 619,321 x 15.25 B; 99,854 x 15.25 B). Whether the per-factor height arrays (JS-8) are in the 15.25 B is not stated.
fatal_flaws: Owner decision D27 (DECISIONS.md:314-323): the design runs in the parked app. Reviving it reverses 'no installer is built' (DECISIONS.md:322-323); ROADMAP Next 15 leaves keep-or-delete to Carson.

Owner decision, AGENTS rule 4: 'Third-party code (Leaflet) and fonts are served by the site, not a CDN' (AGENTS.md:71-72). A loads CesiumJS from cdnjs with SRI (design-a.json library_pin_and_integrity_policy). Amend the rule, or vendor the library, which puts about 6 MB raw into every update (DECISIONS.md:53-59, D6).

Owner decision on reach: the app is localhost-only (desktop/launcher.py:433), so A cannot meet Next 2's phone checks. The decided product direction is the website (DECISIONS.md:353); moving the view there is a new decision against D2.

Owner decision on the no-paid-token constraint: Cesium.js 1.146.0 has 12 'defaultAccessToken' references (live grep). Cesium's docs say 'A default access token is provided for evaluation purposes only' (cesium.com Ion reference, WebFetch 2026-10-17). A ships that token in a production page, and its ion-off claim is untraced (design-a.json unverified).
Owner decision, ROADMAP Next 4: phases 1-3 add GIBS, GOES ACHA, MRMS 3D, NWS radar image and terrain feeds before the predeclared metrics exist (ROADMAP.md:46-48).

scores.name: Design B: separate globe window served by the desktop shell, outside the payload
reasons: O 7: the same globe and storm content as A, in a separate window, with a bundled library and a decode child process (design-b.json components C1-C8). The most literal reading of 'globe', with the most machinery.

P 1: each globe change needs a new installer per OS, distributed by hand from a GitHub Release (design-b.json installer_churn_and_updates). The owner called the app 'too complicated' and wanted it replaced by a website (DECISIONS.md:315). B moves back toward installs. O5: library and decoder bytes ship in every installer even when the view is off.
F 0: a local window on 127.0.0.1 with a random port (design-b.json C1). No phone path; the design never mentions phones.

V 2: a second server, a decode child process and a snapshot table to show the same radar and alerts. The snapshot parity with Live Storms is a real plus (design-b.json data_endpoints C6). Jobs remain parked (DECISIONS.md:324-325).

H 6: 'could not refresh' on a failed request, never an all-clear (G-JS5), and the banner split are good; the not_in_javascript list is a useful rule 4 check. Docked for the same unresolved items as A.
D 1: refuses demo outright ('/globe?event=demo is refused with 400', design-b.json default_off_setting).
Rule 4 (not scored): B is the only design that bundles the library, which satisfies AGENTS.md:71-72 without a rule change. That does not offset P or F.
fatal_flaws: Owner decision D27 and O1 (DECISIONS.md:314-323; design-b.json owner_decisions): the desktop app is parked and no installer is built. B cannot start until a DECISIONS entry names D27 and reverses it.

Owner decision O4 with AGENTS rule 2 and D3: new pip packages (netCDF4, numpy) need a new installer per OS (AGENTS.md:60-64; DECISIONS.md:31-37). Each globe change means installer churn; the owner must accept it or choose a lower-churn variant (design-b.json B2).
Owner decision on reach: no phone path, so it fails Next 2's phone checks unless the view moves to the website.
Owner decision, ROADMAP Next 4: new feeds before predeclared metrics (ROADMAP.md:46-48). And the bundled ion token question shared with A.

honesty_traps: Magnitude reading: A's 3x and 5x exaggeration and B's camera-sized voxels can read as storm height or intensity. C has no 3D.
Uncorrected cloud tops: C's P1 and A's and B's phase 1 draw cloud tops 3-33 km off (parallax.json, via design-c.json). Hold until correction.
Blank read as clear: all three say blank or grey is not clear; the site already says 'Never dry' (gridded.py:192-197; map.js:34-38).

Freshness drift: DESIGN.md:154 says radar is stale past 15 min; DESIGN.md:333 says 30 min; DECISIONS.md:341 says 15 min for the snapshot; website/sources.py:115 uses 30 min for MRMS frames. Pick one per product by DECISIONS entry.
Demo as evidence: A and B exclude demo; C is silent. The label must match rule 5 (base.html:17).
field_reach: A: none (desktop window on 127.0.0.1). B: none (local window). C: the public site returned HTTP 200 for the Now, map and reports pages with a viewport tag (live). No phone has tested the map (DECISIONS.md:402-403; Next 2). DESIGN.md:22-23 assumes a crew lead on a phone; the crew device mix is unmeasured.
demo: Rule 5 allows demo data only under the demo event, labelled DEMO (AGENTS.md:75-76). The site has no demo event; its sample build says 'Sample data' (base.html:17). Two routes give the owner a walkthrough without invented storms: C's layers in the labelled sample build, or archived real replays (evaluation-predeclared.json cases) labelled as archived. The owner decides whether either meets rule 5.
